chunks: Yunus from Ziyad ibn Marwan said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer in the two Sanctuaries, so he said: I love for you what I love for myself – complete the prayer.

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim, a title for Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِتْمَامِ الصَّلَاةِ: Completing the prayer (performing four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries (Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and Masjid al-Nabi in Medina)

ai.seo_question: Should Muslims shorten their prayers when visiting Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Ziyad ibn Marwan seeks the ruling of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the validity of shortening prayers (*Qasr*) within the boundaries of the two holy sanctuaries, Mecca and Medina. The Imam’s response, 'I love for you what I love for myself,' is interpreted by Shia scholars as a strong recommendation (*Istihbab*) to perform the complete four-rak'ah prayer, reflecting the unique spiritual status of these regions where the obligation of shortening is lifted or preferred to be abandoned. This narration underscores the principle that the sanctity of the Harams elevates the prayer to its full form, aligning with the broader Shia jurisprudence on the conditions of *Qasr*.

en.hubeali: Yunus, from Ziyad Bin Marwan who said,
‘I asked Abu Ibrahimasws (7th Ibrahimasws) about Praying the complete Salaat in the two Harrams. So heasws said: Iasws love for youasws what Iasws love for myselfasws – the complete Salaat’.
en.sarwar: 4. Yunus has narrated from Ziyad ibn Marwan who has said the following: “

I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about performing Salat (prayer) in complete form in the two al-Haram (the sacred places), (Masjid al-Haram and Masjid of al-Madinah). He (the Imam) said, ‘I like for you what I like for myself. You should perform Salat (prayer) in complete form.’”
